about: The provider conformance kit's cases and expected answers (T2.5, with T2.6's in-memory fallback), over dataset.sql beside this file, written by T2.5's test author.
Both kit runners read this file and dataset.sql: sdm-testkit's against the rust-host providers, contract/runners/provider_kit.py against each database's Python provider.

Each case is one data request, as the contract spells it (sdm_contract::data::DataRequest), run through the core on the provider under test: the core plans it, asks the provider, reads every page, and admits the answer.

seeds, where given, are the rows of the request's key set, each [key, batch]: a column 'key' of int64 and a column 'batch' of int64, neither null; the runner attaches them and fills the request's 'seeds'.
request_of runs another case's request and seeds; same_as runs another case's request and seeds and expects that case's answer.

capabilities, where given, changes what the provider declares for the case: 'withhold' takes those optional requests out of its declared set, and 'fallback' declares the in-memory fallback's limits (ProviderCapabilities::fallback); left out, the provider declares what it always declares, and no fallback.

inject, where given, makes the provider path fail the request's fetch of that page (page 1 is the first fetch; page 2 the one carrying the first page's continuation) with a provider error of kind data_source, retryable as given.
page_rows: the most rows the provider puts in one page of an answer, for every case.

An answer is compared column by column by name (the columns listed; any other column the provider's answer holds is not compared) and value by value: numbers by value (an integer equals the same float), text as text, null as null. ordered: the rows in order; otherwise as a multiset. count with any_of: exactly that many rows, each one of any_of's, none taken twice.
An error is compared by its code, kind, retryable, and each field listed, as text.

fetched, where given, is every fetch the case makes, by request name, in order, exactly; it stands in for the page counts, and for inject's page being asked (round 1: a fallback past its byte limit on one page asks for no later page).
A float's zero is one value whichever its sign, as SQL compares it: -0.0 equals 0.0 in an answer, a key and a count of distinct values (round 1).

checked: 'hand' answers were worked out by hand from dataset.sql (why says how) and are also recomputed by record.py; 'recorded' answers are record.py's alone. record.py computes every answer from the dataset in plain Python, never through sdm-data's SQL.

faults.name: truncate
faults.what: In the host's provider path, every answer of more than one page ends one page early: the page before the last carries no continuation, so the last page's rows never reach the core and nothing says so.

faults.name: silent_capability
faults.what: In the host's provider path, a provider that declares neighbors answers every neighbors fetch with its statement's columns and no rows, and no error: a declared capability that fails silently.
